title: Denser Planar Color Codes
abstract: We consider the 4.8.8 color code in a brickwork layout on the square lattice with nearest-neighbor gates. We identify periodic superdense circuits with twelve CNOT layers that appear to preserve the full distance of these codes. Including ancillas, the family uses $q=(2d^2+5d-5)/2$ physical qubits for distance $d$: asymptotically $2/3$ as many as the triangular 6.6.6 color code and $1/2$ as many as the rotated surface code at the same code distance. Circuit-level simulations targeting superconducting architectures demonstrate favorable scaling of 4.8.8 color codes at plausible physical noise rates, including both for planar codes and their toroidal cousins under periodic boundary conditions.
summary: This paper analyzes the 4.8.8 color code as a viable quantum memory candidate for superconducting quantum processors. By optimizing its circuit layout and utilizing periodic superdense circuits, the authors demonstrate favorable qubit scaling compared to established codes like the surface code. The work provides detailed circuit-level simulations showing the code's robustness at plausible noise levels.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve quantum memory performance by comparing different topological quantum error-correcting codes and optimizing their circuit implementation on superconducting hardware.
main_result: The 4.8.8 color code, when optimized with a brickwork layout and periodic circuits, is shown to be a competitive quantum memory, exhibiting favorable qubit scaling compared to other codes at the same distance.
method: The authors analyze circuit structures, construct periodic superdense circuits using CNOT layers, and compare qubit overheads and circuit depths for various color codes.
model_or_system: The study focuses on implementing topological quantum error-correcting codes (like 4.8.8 color codes) on the square lattice, modeled for superconducting quantum processors with nearest-neighbor gates.
key_observables: Qubit count ($q$), circuit depth (CNOT layers), logical error rate ($\ell_F$), and physical noise scaling ($p$).
important_parameters: Code distance ($d$), physical noise rate ($p=10^{-3}$), and the specific gate set (SI1000).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of Tesseract decoding and specific circuit optimizations (brickwork layout, superdense extraction) for favorable noise scaling.
figures_summary: Figures compare X/Z memory performance at low noise, show qubit counts for different tilings, and illustrate the spatial repeat structure of the torus circuit.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the 4.8.8 code on a square lattice, detailing the periodic superdense circuit construction, comparing its resource overheads against triangular and surface codes, and analyzing circuit-level noise scaling.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of resource scaling and circuit depth for topological codes is highly relevant for designing fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures.
